Questions, answered
Something we didn’t cover? Drop us a line .
Is there a free plan? You can sign up, connect your calendars, set up your links, and use meeting polls for free. To let people book from your links, you need Basic or Premium.
Is there a free trial? There’s no self-serve trial. Every plan has a 30-day money-back guarantee instead: if SavvyCal isn’t right for you, ask for a full refund within 30 days of paying. If you need to try it with your team first, email support@savvycal.com.
Do people who book with me need an account? No. People who book from your links never need an account or a paid plan. They can also overlay their own calendar on your link for free.

Do you offer volume pricing? Yes. Teams of more than 50 users can email support@savvycal.com to ask about volume pricing.
Can I get a refund? Yes. Ask within 30 days of your first payment for a full refund, no questions asked.
What happens if I cancel? Your subscription stays active until the end of your billing period. After that, we deactivate your links but keep your data, as long as you don’t delete your account.

pages.title: Calendar Overlay: Let People See Their Own Calendar When They Book · SavvyCal
pages.text:
Features Pricing What’s New
Log in Sign up
Let people see their own calendar when they book you.
People booking with you can lay their own calendar over your open times and spot a time that works. Only they see their events, and it’s free for them.
Try SavvyCal risk-free See a live booking page
Overlay my calendar

How does it work for the person booking?
One toggle and a quick sign-in, and their week appears on your link. The gear icon lets them pick which calendars to show.
On phones and in Month View, times that clash with their events get a small red slash instead.
1 Open your link . They open your scheduling link, as they would to book any time.
2 Click “Overlay my calendar” . The toggle sits above the week of open times.
3 Sign in . They sign in with Google, Microsoft, or Fastmail, and come straight back to your link.
4 See their week . Their events appear next to your open times. They can turn them off and on with the same toggle.
5 Pick a time and book . Their name and email are filled in on the booking form, so there’s less to type.
What does the person booking need?
A Google, Microsoft, or Fastmail account to sign in with. If they don’t have a SavvyCal account, signing in creates a free one. It costs them nothing, and it isn’t a trial that runs out.
They don’t need an account to book you. Without overlay, they pick a time and fill in the booking form as usual.
To overlay an iCloud calendar, they sign in with Google, Microsoft, or Fastmail first, then connect iCloud from the gear icon.
Can I see their calendar?
No. Only the person booking sees their events. SavvyCal reads their events from their calendar for the dates on screen, shows them to them, and doesn’t save them to its database.
You see the booking they make, the same as any other booking.
Which plan do I need?
Overlay is on every SavvyCal link, so it comes with Basic: $10 per user per month billed annually, or $12 monthly. Signing up, connecting your calendars, and setting up links is free; letting people book from your links needs a paid plan.
See plans & pricing

Can people see their own calendar while they book with me? Yes. On a SavvyCal link, the person booking clicks “Overlay my calendar” and signs in with Google, Microsoft, or Fastmail. Their events then appear next to your open times.
Does the person booking need a SavvyCal account? Signing in to overlay creates a free SavvyCal account if they don’t have one. It costs them nothing, and they don’t need it to book you without overlay.
Can I see their calendar? No. Only the person booking sees their events. SavvyCal reads them from their calendar for the dates on screen and doesn’t save them to its database.
Does overlay work on phones and embedded links? On phones and in Month View, a signed-in person sees a small red slash on any time that conflicts with their events, instead of the full overlay. Links embedded in a website usually don’t offer overlay, so share your booking page link when it matters.
Which plan do I need? Overlay is on every SavvyCal link, so it comes with Basic: $10 per user per month billed annually, or $12 monthly. Letting people book from your links needs a paid plan.

SavvyCal lets you add buffers around meetings, cap bookings per day, week, or month, require minimum notice, limit how far ahead people can book, and highlight the times you’d rather meet. Every control on this page is on the Basic plan, $10 per user per month billed annually.

Availability controls in SavvyCal
Control What it does Options Where you set it
Buffers Keeps time free before and after each new meeting, next to any busy event on your calendars 0 minutes to 4 hours, before and after Per link, with account defaults
Minimum notice Stops bookings that start too soon 0 minutes to 4 weeks Per link
Booking window Limits how many days ahead people can book Any number of days Per link
Fixed date range Only offers times within set dates On or after, on or before, or between dates; several ranges Per link
Frequency limits Caps how many meetings can be booked One or more limits per day, week, or month Per link, or across all your links
Preferred times Shows your preferred times first, marked “Best” Automatic (batch meetings together, prefer mornings or afternoons) or a saved schedule Per link, for links with one host
Time blocks Marks you available when a calendar event with a certain name exists Title equals or contains a word Per schedule
Overrides Blocks or opens time on specific dates Block or allow; allow can ignore conflicts, notice, and limits Per schedule (every link using it) or per link
Schedules Different weekly hours for different links Unlimited saved schedules, or custom hours on one link Per link
Start times How often slots start Every 15, 20, 30, or 60 minutes Per link
Time zone changes Moves your availability to another time zone for set dates Date range and time zone Account settings
Last-minute change lock Stops the person who booked from rescheduling or canceling close to the start 15 minutes to 1 week before Per link
How to control when people book you
Can I add buffer time between meetings?
Yes. Set a buffer before and after meetings on each link, up to 4 hours, or set defaults for new links. Buffers apply next to every busy event on your connected calendars, not only meetings booked through SavvyCal.
Read the help doc
Can I limit how many meetings I get per day, week, or month?
Yes. Add one or more frequency limits to a link, such as 3 per day and 10 per week. To cap meetings across all your links, set account-wide limits in Settings. Limits count meetings booked through SavvyCal.
Read the help doc
Can I stop people from booking at the last minute?
Yes. Minimum notice sets how much lead time a booking needs, from a few minutes up to 4 weeks. Set it to 24 hours, for example, to stop same-day bookings.
Read the help doc
Can I limit how far ahead people can book?
Yes. Turn on a booking window to only show the next so many days, such as 30. You can also limit a link to fixed dates, such as on or after September 1, or between two dates. With minimum notice, you can offer only times between 14 and 30 days out.
Read the help doc
Can I steer people toward the times I prefer?
Yes. Turn on preferred times, and the booking page shows those times first, marked “Best”. People can still see your other open times. SavvyCal can choose preferred times for you, near your other meetings or in the morning or afternoon, or you can pick a saved schedule of preferred hours inside your wider hours.
Read the help doc
How do I protect focus time?
Put your focus time on your calendar as a busy event. SavvyCal checks every connected calendar, and busy events block booking on all your links. Events marked free, and events you’ve declined, don’t. To keep long stretches free, batch meetings together with preferred times and add a daily limit.
Read the help doc
Can I use calendar events to set when I’m available?
Yes. With time blocks, any calendar event with a name you choose, such as “Office hours”, becomes time people can book. Busy events inside a time block still block it, unless the time block’s name includes [Force].
Read the help doc
How do I block vacation days or specific dates?
Block the dates on a schedule, and every link that uses that schedule is blocked. You can also block time on a single link. Or add an all-day event marked busy to your calendar, which blocks every link that checks that calendar.
Read the help doc
Can different links have different hours?
Yes. Save as many schedules as you need, such as “Work hours” and “Client calls”, and choose one for each link, or set custom hours on a single link.
Can I stop people from rescheduling or canceling at the last minute?
Yes. Turn on “Prevent last-minute changes” on a link and choose how early the lock starts, from 15 minutes to a week before the meeting. It applies to the person who booked. You can still reschedule or cancel up to the start time.

What if I’m traveling to another time zone?
Schedule a time zone change for the dates you’re away, and your availability moves to that time zone for those dates.

What SavvyCal doesn’t do
Travel time between locations SavvyCal doesn’t add travel time based on where meetings are. If you add travel time to an event in Apple Calendar on a connected iCloud calendar, SavvyCal counts it as busy.
Limits on meetings in a row You can’t cap consecutive meetings. Buffers keep a gap after every meeting, and daily limits cap the total.
Holidays SavvyCal doesn’t block public holidays for you. Block them on your schedule, or add busy all-day events to your calendar.
Limits that count other calendar events Frequency limits count meetings booked through SavvyCal, not other events on your calendar.
Preferred times on links with several hosts Preferred times work on links with one host, not on collective or round robin links with several.

Can SavvyCal add travel time between meetings? Not based on location. If you add travel time to an event in Apple Calendar on a connected iCloud calendar, SavvyCal counts it as busy.
Can I limit back-to-back meetings? You can’t cap how many meetings happen in a row. Use buffers to keep a gap after each meeting, and a daily limit to cap the total.
Does SavvyCal block holidays automatically? No. Block holiday dates on your schedule, or add busy all-day events to your calendar.
